title: Six spectral regions lack the reported 63 km/s shift in four GJ 357 HARPS exposures
abstract: Four GJ 357 HARPS exposures have catalog velocities about 63 km/s below normal. Prior work found no such shift in H-alpha. We test six other spectral regions against a normal observed template. All 24 primary fits give relative shifts from -0.370 to +0.194 km/s, while the catalog predicts -63.550 to -62.522 km/s. Free shifts reduce squared residuals by 60 to 98 percent against fits near the catalog shift. Three continuum filters retain the result. A normal control has small shifts, and 48 imposed-shift tests recover plus or minus 63 km/s to within 0.011 km/s. This supports a failed velocity measurement across many spectral lines. The exact pipeline fault remains open. The tests share HARPS extraction and calibration. They do not exclude a faint blended component or test the known planets. The package includes code, aggregate evidence, exact source hashes and external retrieval steps.

display.caption: Six regions exclude H-alpha. Left: primary velocity ranges across four suspect spectra and the catalog shift range. Right: minimum SSE reduction across those spectra for each continuum filter. Ranges are not confidence intervals.

citations.reason: We reuse its external frozen spectra and catalog and test its H-alpha conclusion with six other spectral regions and two new normal spectra.
Our multi-region test supports its interpretation of four extreme DRS velocities as a data quality concern.
